errors.text: The proposed oxygen target of <0.1 wt.% contradicts the target process, in which controlled oxygen near 1.0 wt.% provides interstitial strengthening while quenching prevents alpha-HCP embrittlement.

The intervention is replaced by high-pressure hot extrusion and aging rather than 3D ink extrusion, hydrogen de-binding, and prolonged vacuum sintering at 1400 °C for 18 hours with a titanium-sponge getter.
The proposed 400–500 °C rapid decomposition step does not reconstruct the sequential hydride decomposition and in-situ alloying pathway governed by hydride formation enthalpies.
The essential water quench from 1500 °C used to retain metastable beta-BCC is omitted and replaced by an arbitrary cooling-rate threshold followed by aging.
B2 or Laves-type coherent precipitation is speculative for HfNbTaTiZr and is inferred from a compositionally and structurally dissimilar W-Ni-Fe-Ta alloy; Laves phases may instead be brittle.
The hypothesis omits the silicide coating and self-healing Zr/Hf oxide mechanism responsible for the large reduction in oxidation rate.
